events.title: Flood near Weiant
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Licking County. A teenage girl drowned after being trapped under debris in fast flowing water.

events.title: Flood near Englewood
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Montgomery County. The body of a man was recovered in the Stillwater River after the man entered the Englewood Recreational Reservoir water and did not resurface.

events.title: Flash Flood near South Bloomingville
events.description: 1 death. Hocking County. Hocking Hills State Park reported that a tree fell onto a hiker in Conkles Hollow State Nature Preserve. The cause was estimated to be hillside instability due to several days of moderate to heavy rainfall.

events.title: Lightning near Minerva Park
events.description: 1 death. Franklin County. A person was struck and killed by lightning.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Akron
events.description: 1 death. Summit County. Weakened tree fell onto home in Akron and killed occupant. Thunderstorm was likely sub-severe per radar data. The nearby Akron-Fulton International Airport ASOS recorded a peak convective wind gust of 44 mph at 9:26 AM EST. No other reports of thunderstorm-related damage or severe convective weather were received as the cluster of storms moved through the Akron area.

events.title: Flash Flood near Manchester
events.description: 1 death. Adams County. Island creek quickly rose out of its banks. A vehicle was swept into the water on Island Creek Road, resulting in one fatality. M17IW.

events.title: Flood near Grandview
events.description: 1 death. Washington County. The Ohio River gauge at Willow Island Lock rose above its flood stage on the morning of April 3rd, then reached a crest of around 41.3 feet the morning of the 5th. The river then receded below flood stage the next morning. With the river spilling out of its banks, water inundated Ohio Route 7 in the Reno area. Ohio State Route 7, Township Road 443, and Township Road 19 at Newell Run and Lenards Landing flooded.||During the time the river was out of its banks, a 42 year old man perished after attempting to drive through the floodwaters on State Route 7 just north of Archer Fork Road.

events.title: Tornado near Lakeview Van Horn Ar
events.description: 3 deaths. Logan County. The tornado began in Auglaize County at 1829EST, 3 miles north of Botkins and moved east-southeast, entering Logan County at 1843EST, just north of Santa Fe. Areas of signifincant tree damage occurred along the path of the tornado across northwest Logan County. ||The tornado strengthened as it approached the village of Lakeview, producing severe damage over much of the Lakeview area, beginning along Pine Street and Poplar Court. On Poplar Court, one single family residence was destroyed, with all walls collapsed. A corridor of severe damage continued directly southeast across Main Street,…

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Ohio City
events.description: 1 death. Van Wert County. Emergency management officials reported a large tree fell onto a house and roof of a patio near the intersection of SR 118 and Hoffman St. An husband and wife were under the roof of the porch at the time and had to be rescued. The husband escaped with no injuries, but his 87 year old wife was transported to the hospital and pronounced dead.

events.title: Flood near Crosswick
events.description: 1 death. Warren County. High water was reported in the Waynesville area. An 11 year old boy was killed when he fell into a flooded ditch. M11IW.

events.title: Lightning near Sidney
events.description: 1 death. Shelby County. A truck driver was killed by lightning along I-75 while fixing a mechanical issue with his truck. M50OU.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Clendening
events.description: 2 deaths. Harrison County. More info: https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/2020/11/17/bodies-missing-michigan-hunters-found-clendening-lake-ohio/6322047002/||Two men, aged 43 and 60 and residents of south central Michigan, died when an overloaded watercraft, convective wind, and not being prepared for the environmental conditions all played a role in capsizing their boat. Most likely, based on available information, they were very low in the water and became swamped by high wave action. This resulted in them going into the water, and with no personal flotation devices, they succumbed to hyperthermia and drowned.

events.title: Flash Flood near Price Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Franklin County. A stranded vehicle along Hamilton Road was swept away in rising flood waters, leading to a fatality. F48VE.

events.title: Flash Flood near Unionvale
events.description: 2 deaths. Harrison County. Numerous areas experienced flooding across Harrison, Carroll, and Tuscarawas county. One and half to three inches of rain occurred in parts of Eastern Ohio. ||Two individuals died in flooded cars near swollen creeks. events.title: Flood near Thurman
events.description: 1 death. Gallia County. Multiple roads were closed across the county due to flooding, including State Route 325, State Route 233, and State Route 141. On the evening of the 14th, a 73 year old man drowned in the flood waters at the intersection of State Route 141 and German Ridge Road. The man drove his car into the high water and was overcome by the rushing water.

events.title: Lightning near Cummingsville
events.description: 2 deaths. Hamilton County. Three women were jogging in Spring Grove Cemetery when a thunderstorm rolled in. The women took cover under a large oak tree, but all three women were hit when lightning struck. One women was killed immediately, the other two were injured. A second women passed away five days later. F27UT. F55UT.

events.title: Flash Flood near Beunquat
events.description: 1 death. Wyandot County. Spring Branch Run in Eden Township washed away portion of Township Highway 136/Route 36. A motorists drove into the flood waters and the vehicle was swept approximately 100 years to the west where a passenger perished. One fatality reported at 1:20 AM from a vehicle driving into the washout.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Crestview
events.description: 1 death. Lucas County. There was significant tree damage reported. Heavy industrial parts and storage containers were lifted and tossed in the air. A man in the town of Holland was killed when an uprooted tree fell on the car while he was sitting in the vehicle.

events.title: Tornado near Durbin
events.description: 1 death. Mercer County. The tornado appeared to have first touched down west of Celina, near the intersection of Township Line Road and Bunker Hill Road, where about half of a barn's metal roof was removed and strewn in a narrow path to the east-northeast. At least two other barns also lost nearly half of their metal roofing in the vicinity of Bunker Hill Road. Numerous trees in this area, with trunk diameters of 18 to 24 inches, were also snapped and blown down in various directions. This type of damage was consistent with wind speeds of up to 90 mph and associated with an EF1 tornado. ||The next damage occurred to…

events.title: Tornado near Pyrmont
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Montgomery County. The tornado initially touched down just west of Brookville and areas on the south side of Brookville sustained heavy damage, consistent with high-end EF2 wind speeds. Numerous homes suffered significant roof damage and removal, including exterior wall collapse and complete garage destruction. ||The tornado then carved a path east through Trotwood where damage consistent with EF2 wind speeds was widespread and some homes sustained damage consistent with EF3 wind speeds. Structures here again featured roof removal and exterior wall collapse. This was particularly true on the south side of…

events.title: Flood near Idaho
events.description: 1 death. Pike County. The body of a man was found near his vehicle on Ohio Route 124, near the intersection of Ohio Route 772. The vehicle was found almost 700 feet inside signs placed in the roadway marking the road closed. Water inside the vehicle indicated that is had been at least half submerged in water. M58VE.

events.title: Flood near Mt Blanco
events.description: 1 death. Meigs County. Multiple roads were closed due to high water across central and western Meigs County. This included State Route 681 along the West Branch of the Shade River and State Route 124 along Thomas Fork. Leading Creek also flooded, closing parts of Leading Creek Road and State Route 124. A 54 year old man drowned in the flood waters along Leading Creek around 6 PM on the 6th. The man drove his car into the high water and became stranded. He abandoned the car and tried to make it to dry land but was swept away by the water.

events.title: Flood near Massieville
events.description: 1 death. Ross County. Trego Creek was running high due to recent heavy rains. An 8 year old boy drowned after being swept away in the creek. M8IW.

events.title: Flood near Pasco
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Shelby County. Three children were playing by Mosquito Creek. The bank of Mosquito Creek gave way and a boy fell into the creek and drowned. M6IW.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Windfall
events.description: 1 death. Medina County. A vehicle traveling down River Styx Road near Interstate 71 was struck by a falling tree knocked down by thunderstorm wind gusts. The tree land on the front half of the passenger cabin killing the 28 year old mother driving. Her baby in the back seat was not injured.

events.title: Lightning near North Brewster
events.description: 1 death. Stark County. An 82 year old man was struck by lightning and killed while working outside. This incident occurred just outside of Brewster.

events.title: Lightning near Warsaw
events.description: 1 death. Coshocton County. Local media reported a 9 year old boy was struck by lightning and later died. The boy was outside attempting to bring horses into a barn when he was struck.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Roachester
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Warren County. A man jumped into the Little Miami River in Morrow after fleeing a house fire. He was swept away and killed (indirect fatality) as the river was running very high from earlier heavy rainfall.

events.title: Flash Flood near Eastwood
events.description: 3 deaths. Brown County. Thunderstorms developed across Brown County around 2100EST. A rain gauge near Red Oak received 2.4 inches of rain between 2120EST and 2205EST. Flooding started in the Georgetown area around 2140EST, when 6 people were stranded in multiple vehicles along State Route 125 due to rapidly rising water on Straight Creek. Over the next hour, numerous water rescues occurred throughout much of Brown County. By 2220EST, 3.0 inches of rain had fallen at the Red Oak gauge. Between 2200EST and 2300EST, Red Oak Creek rapidly rose out of its banks and caused widespread damage to homes and roads along the…

events.title: Flood near Oregonia
events.description: 1 death. Warren County. A 72 year old woman drove her car into the Little Miami River from a parking area along Cold Springs Road. The woman was pulled from the car by rescuers but was later pronounced dead at the hospital.

events.title: Flood near Oregonia
events.description: 1 death. Warren County. A 72 year old woman drove her car into the Little Miami River from a parking area along Cold Springs Road. The woman was pulled from the car by rescuers but was later pronounced dead at the hospital.
